newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Eminis to expand capacity by 50 pc.
newsitem.headline: Turk Eminis to expand capacity by 50 pc.

text.p: Turkey's leading tin and plastic packages producer Eminis Ambalaj Sanayi ve TIcaret A.S. will expand its output capacity by 50 percent with investments to be completed this year, a senior company official said.

"The total capacity will increase by 50 percent, but the real increase will be 100 percent with new products to be produced during the idle seasons," Mehmet Ozbalak, the company's internal auditor, told Reuters.
The company currently produces paint packages mainly for the sister company Marshall Boya and aims to shift to new products to spread production throughout the year.
"We do not want to give more details on the new product for competitive reasons," he said.
Company shares closed at 16,750 lira on Monday, up from Friday's 16,500 lira on the Istanbul Stock Exchange although the market index lost 2.42 percent to end at 1,532.
Eminis reported 1.2 trillion lira of total sales in 1996 against 586 billion lira in 1995 and increased its net profit to 123 billion lira from previous 87 billion.
Its interest payments jumped to 135.3 billion lira last year from 34.4 billion in 1995, because of the capacity expansion and modernisation investments.
Ozbalak said their sale target was to reduce the share of sales to Marshall to below 50 percent of the total to reduce dependence on the sister company.

The company raised its turnover to $15 million in 1996 with a four percent output increase over 1995's 17.4 million units of paint packages, which included 12.4 million tin and 4.9 million plastic ones.
Eminis built production lines for 10 kilogram plastic packages last year by spending 600,000 Deutsche marks. A five million mark new factory building is expected to be finished this year.
"As a result of the higher capacities and new products, Eminis will continue to grow in 1997. We have a market share of around 30 percent," Ozbalak said.

He said the per capita consumption of tin packages was only 0.7 kilogram and plastic packages was 1.2 kilograms in Turkey, compared to eight and 10 kilograms, respectively in the U.S. last year, which showed the future potential of the domestic market.
